messages:
Maria Gomez: quick heads-up — nightly MLPerf-ish run flagged a regression on workspace sizing. two configs hit OOMs and one saw +15% tail latency. looks related to attention/ffn kernel selection fallback.

Kevin Lee: I dug into the profiler. when FlashAttention path selects Triton fallback (for certain seq/batch combos) memory footprint jumps. rough summary from the run:
```
Model: custom-llama-13b
Seq: 2048, Batch: 4
Kernel path: flashattn_v2 -> deterministic fallback -> triton_attn
Observed delta: +1.1GB GPU mem on fallback (attention), +0.6GB from cublaslt at FFN for these shapes
KV cache: steady but allocations spike during kernel transitions
Allocator: slab32 fragmentation increased (slab reclaim not triggering quickly)
```

Sree Patel: that matches something I saw last month — when kernel chooser flips to triton_attn we don't reuse the flash workspace and end up allocating an extra slab-aligned buffer for the fallback. two ideas: 1) add a per-kernel "workspace_cap" that enforces reuse of existing slabs before fresh alloc, 2) prefer cuBLASLt-packed FFN kernels for these shapes to avoid extra temp buffers.

Devon Clark: +1. also the allocator currently snaps slab size based on the max historical reserve which makes rare fallbacks reserve large chunks permanently. propose a soft-eviction window: if a kernel fallback hasn't occurred in X minutes reduce its reserved slab to Y%. that should reduce long-tail memory.

Kevin Lee: experiment results from a quick patch where I set workspace_safety_margin_pct=10 for triton_attn: OOMs stopped for seq=2048/batch=4 but tail latency increased ~3% because we throttled some batching. tradeoff is tolerable for now. attaching perf snippet: 
```
patch: set workspace_safety_margin_pct=10 for triton_attn
nightly: no OOMs, tail p95 +3%, avg cost -2%
```

Maria Gomez: interesting. we need deterministic rule for kernel chooser: avoid choosing triton if it forces new large allocations unless latency benefit > X and memory delta < Y. can we compute memory_delta_estimate cheaply at routing time?

Sree Patel: yes — we can maintain per-kernel cost model: (expected_workspace_bytes, expected_temp_buffers). use sampling from profiler runs to update. cheap lookup at request time: if workspace_delta > threshold block kernel selection or prefer packed-cublaslt. also track sequence-length distribution so we only apply for rare long-seq cases.

Devon Clark: for implementation I'd add two knobs: 
- kernel_workspace_budget_override: explicit per-model override for worst-case shapes
- dynamic_reclaim_window_sec: how long allocator holds onto reserves from rare fallbacks

Example config snippet: 
```
"kernel_profiles": {
  "triton_attn": { "est_workspace": 1_400_000_000, "safety_margin_pct": 10 },
  "flashattn_v2": { "est_workspace": 300_000_000 }
}
"allocator": { "dynamic_reclaim_window_sec": 300 }
```

Kevin Lee: another small perf note: when FFN uses cuBLASLt with matmul splitting it allocates GEMM workspace per-split. switching to the fused Triton-FFN reduces allocations but increases compute. for cost-sensitive tiers prefer fused path; for latency-critical prefer cuBLASLt if it doesn't increase memory.

runtime-bot: nightly-bench finished: <https://redwood.internal/bench/1719999999|nightly-mlperf-1719999999>. results attached.

Maria Gomez: ok action items: 
- Kevin: add quick estimator lookup (profiler-derived) and a guard that avoids kernel selection if est_workspace_delta > 800MB for this model (assign: kevin)
- Sree: prototype dynamic_reclaim_window and make default 300s for now (assign: sree)
- Devon: run shard-level MLPerf-like sweep with both knobs toggled and collect p95/p99 + OOM counts (assign: devon)

Maria Gomez: timeline — can we get a short experiment run by EOD tomorrow? even just 10 iterations to validate OOM fixes. ping me if you need help reproducing. :thumbsup:

Kevin Lee: got it. starting estimator today. will post a profiler snippet once ready.

Sree Patel: will branch reclaim change now.

Devon Clark: I'll queue a sweep on the bench fleet and include both Flash/Triton/cuBLASLt variants.

Maria Gomez: thanks team. updating the incident doc briefly and linking here: <https://redwood.internal/incidents/1872|OOM-workspace-sizing-1719999999>
